  [DOC] “Alaska Air Group… Total operating revenue: FY2022 $9,646M, FY2023 $10,426M, FY2024 $11,735M.” [DOC-1]

Scope change (Alaska – Hawaiian acquisition):

[DOC] “On September 18, 2024, Alaska Air Group completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings, Inc.… The results of Hawaiian are included in the consolidated financial statements beginning September 18, 2024.… For the period from the acquisition date to December 31, 2024, revenue… from Hawaiian… was $869 million…” [DOC-2]

Step 2 – Compute growth and “momentum”

Year-over-year revenue growth rates (approximate):

- Delta

  - 2023→2024: (61,643 − 58,048) / 58,048 ≈ 6.2%

- United  
  - 2022→2023: (53,717 − 44,955) / 44,955 ≈ 19.5%  
  - 2023→2024: (57,063 − 53,717) / 53,717 ≈ 6.2%

- Southwest  
  - 2022→2023: (26,091 − 23,814) / 23,814 ≈ 9.6%  
  - 2023→2024: (27,483 − 26,091) / 26,091 ≈ 5.3%

- American  
  - 2022→2023: (52,788 − 48,971) / 48,971 ≈ 7.8%  
  - 2023→2024: (54,211 − 52,788) / 52,788 ≈ 2.7%

- Alaska (note: 2024 includes Hawaiian from Sept 18)  
  - 2022→2023: (10,426 − 9,646) / 9,646 ≈ 8.1%  
  - 2023→2024: (11,735 − 10,426) / 10,426 ≈ 12.5%, but this is boosted by ~$869M of Hawaiian revenue only in 2024. [DOC-2]

Step 3 – Assess “strongest revenue growth momentum”

Interpreting “momentum” as the *sustained* or improving growth rate into 2024, and focusing on organic comparability:

- Delta and United: very strong 2022→2023 rebounds (≈15–20%) that slow to ≈6.2% in 2024, but still deliver the highest 2024 growth among the large carriers on a like-for-like basis.
- Southwest: moderating to ≈5.3% in 2024.
- American: weakest 2024 growth at ≈2.7%.
- Alaska: headline 12.5% in 2024, but this overstates underlying momentum because it includes incremental Hawaiian revenue that was not present in prior years; the scope change makes its 2023→2024 growth not directly comparable to the others. [DOC-2]

Among the airlines without material scope changes, United shows the highest two-year compound growth and shares the strongest 2023→2024 growth rate (≈6.2%) with Delta, starting from a lower 2022 base, indicating somewhat stronger underlying momentum in scaling revenue.

ANSWER: United Airlines
